name: Tower Bridge and the Thames
context: A bascule bridge built from 1886 to 1894 next to the Tower of London, to let ships reach the busiest port in the world. Its construction was one of the most photographed of the Victorian era.

archives.title: Tower Bridge RMG PW0707
archives.description: Tower Bridge An atmospheric late drypoint in which Wyllie uses a variety of techniques to capture the scale and the scope of activity on the working river. The industrial nature of the Thames is highlighted by the crowded and heavily etched shoreline, the raised Tower bridge, and the crane at work at the foreground of the image. Here he has used an upright composition that he may have learnt from Whistler many years before. The work is signed 'W L Wyllie', lower left. For another version, see PAF2220. W. L. archives.title: Fonds Achille Dassonville (1890-1967) - Royaume-Uni - Londres - Vue sur le Tower Bridge depuis les quais de la Tamise (MédiHAL 5131839)
archives.artist: Maison Méditerranéenne Des Sciences de l'Homme Phonothèque, Achille Fernand Hector Dassonville
archives.description: The photograph shows two women sitting on a wide stone bench and a child standing on the cobbled, tree-lined embankment of the River Thames. The view is taken opposite Tower Bridge, near the Tower of London. On the embankment are some exhibition cannons. The woman in the foreground, probably Blanche Clarke Bathurst, is wearing a hat and gloves, dressed in 1920s fashion, and is posing, looking into the camera. At the other end of the bench, another woman is reading. The child, looking into the camera, seems to be waiting for her.
